presentation.label: 8-bit sampler
presentation.summary: Plays a Flex sample like an 8-bit tracker: gritty, held samples and a cyclic stretch that pulls pitch and time apart.
presentation.overview: Amiga is a track machine modelled on how a home computer's 8-bit sound chip and its tracker software played samples. It plays the track's Flex sample through the stock reader, reduces its word length and storage rate before the Octatrack repitches it, and can restart the sample every few milliseconds a little further on, so PTCH changes the pitch and SPD the length. RATE is stock's own, forwards and backwards. The track's filter, AMP, LFOs and effects follow as for any sample.
highlights: SPD sets how fast the note moves through the sample and GRN the cycle, 96 to 4128 samples: half speed, about twice as fast or a held sound, at any pitch.
STR can turn the stretch into a pitch shift of up to an octave either way.
RATE is stock's own: forwards, backwards and slower, with the stretch following it both ways.
SRR lowers the storage rate, BITS sets the word from 16 to 4 bits (8 by default), LED adds a fixed lowpass.
RATE, SPD and GRN take parameter locks, LFOs and scenes, as SRC knobs do.
usage: Double-tap a track key (or open SRC SETUP), move to AMIGA in the machine list and press YES.
Double-tap the track key again and pick a sample from the Flex list, as for a Flex track.
Open SRC: knob D is RATE, E is SPD, F is GRN.

controls.name: RATE
controls.doc: Stock's RATE, -64 to +63: speed and pitch together, backwards below 0. The stretch follows it both ways. SRC knob D.

controls.name: SPD
controls.doc: How fast the note moves through the sample, whatever the pitch: 64 is its own speed, 32 half, 0 holds. SRC knob E.

controls.name: GRN
controls.doc: The stretch's cycle, 96 to 4128 samples; 1120 by default. SRC knob F.

controls.name: LED
controls.doc: A fixed two-pole lowpass on the stored sample. SRC SETUP knob C.

controls.name: SRR
controls.doc: Storage rate: 16/(16+SRR) of the sample's own, each stored sample an average, then held. SRC SETUP knob D.

controls.name: STR
controls.doc: The stretch: OFF plays as FLEX, ON stretches, PCH shifts the pitch by SPD at the note's own length. SRC SETUP knob E.

controls.name: BITS
controls.doc: Word length from 4 to 16 bits; the saved value is bits minus 4. SRC SETUP knob F.

limitations: USB only: it loads on the Modwerk base over USB (it needs the base's machine list and START dispatch) and has no card build.
Experimental: played and measured on one MKII on a development base; TESTING.md lists what was not tried.

On an MKII one Amiga track beside seven FLEX tracks added 5.5 points to the frame interrupt at the defaults and up to 13.8 with PTCH +12, SRR and LED; eight Amiga tracks reached the base's frame guard, which skipped 17 % of their renders (dropouts). Count on a few Amiga tracks, not eight.
With a USB recording running as well, one Amiga track at PTCH +12 with SRR and LED on beside seven FLEX tracks froze the unit until a power cycle.
No stock RTRG or RTIM on an Amiga track: SPD and GRN take their knobs.
Stock's own time-stretch (TSTR) is off on an Amiga track, and SETUP's LEN switch is LED: the track always uses stock's default length setting.
SRR, LED, STR and BITS are SETUP values: one for the Part, without locks or LFOs.
A sliced track (SLIC on) is not stretched; SRR, BITS and LED still work.
The cycle length is in samples, not tied to the tempo.
A stretched note that is not looped ends when SPD has carried it to the end of the sample, even if LEN would stop a FLEX note sooner by time.
A project opened without the module plays Amiga tracks as FLEX and reads SPD and GRN as stock's RTRG and RTIM, and LED, SRR, STR and BITS as SETUP's LEN, RATE, TSTR and TSNS.
Leaving Amiga for another machine puts the track's SRC settings back to FLEX defaults.
Before a trial of the module ends or the module is removed, put its tracks on another machine: the base refuses to take a machine away from a track that names it.

storage.label: Module image and memory
storage.conditions: The USB package of this source (SHA-256 18cef8b2d5d9152fd12d85d8ca607821776587b6f5b87868f7984eec02373ff3, built by npm run module:dev -- amiga --build-only): 10,652 bytes of code and data and 67,308 of bss, most of it the eight voices' frame memories (8 KB each). The loader's own record for the module and the stack the render uses are not counted. The loader allows a module 128 KiB.

processing.label: ColdFire, in the frame interrupt
processing.display: Not measured in cycles; 5.5 to 13.8 points of a frame a track
processing.conditions: No worst case in cycles exists. On the owner's MKII (development twin d8fae687 of the base, 11 November 2026; five seconds of a 131 BPM pattern, eight tracks playing loops, one reading each) the frame interrupt read 63.7 % with eight FLEX tracks, 69.2 % with track 1 on Amiga at the defaults and 77.5 % with PTCH +12, SRR and LED; eight Amiga tracks at the defaults read 79.2 % with 16.9 % of their renders skipped by the base's frame guard. These are means over five seconds, not a longest frame. ot_emu counts 300 to 5,355 instructions of the engine's own code per audio frame of one track (worst frame 6,501), which the unit's time did not follow.

impact.conditions: One Amiga track playing a loop beside seven FLEX tracks on an MKII, from the defaults to PTCH +12 with SRR and LED on, and eight Amiga tracks at the defaults. CPU from frame-interrupt readings on the unit (means, one reading each); memory from the package's sizes, all eight voices included whether used or not.

cpu.rationale: The ColdFire reworks the track's source frames in the frame interrupt: the word and rate reduction, the lowpass and the cyclic restarts with their fades. Against a FLEX track on the same unit one Amiga track added 5.5 points of the frame at the defaults and 13.8 with PTCH +12, SRR and LED; eight at the defaults reached the base's 80 % frame guard, which skipped 16.9 % of their renders. Worst-case cycles are not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP program, effect slot or DSP state is added. The reworked frames go to the DSP through the stock FLEX path, which repitches and filters them as it does a FLEX track's.

memory.rationale: 10,652 bytes of code and data and 67,308 of bss in the package, about 76 KiB of the 128 KiB the loader allows a module. Most is eight frame memories of 8 KB, one a track, reserved once at install whether or not a track uses Amiga. No sample RAM is taken and no stock buffer is reused.

tests.summary: Host gate on the engine (verify.py, 56 checks), sample-for-sample comparison with the first build played on a unit, an emulator count of its instructions (bench.py), and RAM trials on the owner's MKII on a development base, 11 November 2026: pages, the stretch both ways, cost beside seven FLEX tracks. Worst-case cycles are not measured; no stock benchmark under a MIDI flood and no flood ran. TESTING.md lists what was not tried.
gates: python3 -B bench.py --emulator <ot_emu> --main <a MAIN image the emulator boots> --output <new private folder>

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Put a drum loop on an Amiga track and play it. At the defaults it is the loop at 8 bits.
Turn PTCH up a few semitones: the loop keeps its length and starts to flutter. Turn GRN for the size of the flutter.
Turn SPD down to 32 for half speed at the same pitch, or all the way to 0 to hold the sound where it is.
Turn RATE below 0: the loop runs backwards, still stretched.
On SRC SETUP, turn SRR up to about 20 for a grainy, folded top end, and switch LED on to take the edge off it.

access.location: The track's machine list (double-tap TRACK, or SRC SETUP)
steps: Double-tap a track key, choose AMIGA in the machine list and press YES, then double-tap again and pick a Flex sample.
On SRC, turn PTCH: the pitch moves and the length stays. Turn SPD (knob E) for the length and GRN (knob F) for the flutter; RATE (knob D) is stock's, backwards below 0.
On SRC SETUP, raise SRR for a lower sample rate. LED, STR and BITS are beside it.
